# Skins (not part of the original)

A skin is a folder of replacement images layered over the original art by the
[hires renderer](/hires). `--param skin=<name>[,<name2>...]` stacks them: later skins win, and any tile or
sprite no skin provides is drawn from the original art. Skins work at every hires scale, including
`hires=1` (the hires renderer then runs at 640 x 480 just to show the skins). Without `skin=` nothing
changes.

```sh
# the sample skin of this repository (assets/skins/sample, generated by tools/make-sample-skin.py)
gasm-run opengta.wasm --asset-dir GTA --asset-dir skins=assets/skins \
  --param intro=0 --param mission=1 --param hires=2 --param skin=sample
# two skins: mine over the sample
gasm-run opengta.wasm --asset-dir GTA --asset-dir skins=my-skins --param hires=4 --param skin=sample,mine
```

Skins are read as files `skins/<name>/...`. With gasm, a second `--asset-dir` with the prefix `skins=`
(gasm's `--asset-dir [prefix=]dir`, see its ABI "Folders") makes a folder of skins appear there; a
`skins/` folder inside the game folder works too. The gasm backend reads skins straight from the assets,
so they also work when the game comes from the installer's cabinets. Natively they go through the file
layer (`hires_skin_reader`, default `vfs_read_all`). The browser player has no way to add a skin folder
yet.

## Layout

```
skins/<name>/skin.ini
skins/<name>/style<NNN>/side/<n>.png        side tile n
skins/<name>/style<NNN>/lid/<n>.png         lid tile n
skins/<name>/style<NNN>/aux/<n>.png         aux tile n (the frames tile animations show)
skins/<name>/style<NNN>/sprite/<n>.png      sprite n
```

- `skin.ini`: `name = ...`, `author = ...`, `scale = N` (the hires scale the art is made for; logged,
  informative). Lines starting with `;` or `#` are comments. A skin without `skin.ini` is skipped with a
  message.
- `style<NNN>`: the style number, `style001` (Liberty City), `style002` (San Andreas), `style003` (Vice
  City).
- Numbers are the style's own: side tiles 0..sides-1, lids 0..lids-1, aux tiles 0..aux-1, as the map
  and `Style_UpdateAnims` use them (an animated lid shows aux tiles: replace those too, or the animation
  shows the original frames); sprite numbers are the game's (the index into the sprite info table, as
  `Sprite.frame` holds them; car info records add their group base, see [Sprites](/sprites)).
- Images: PNG, 8 bits per channel, RGBA, RGB, palette (with `tRNS` transparency), grey or grey + alpha,
  not interlaced. Other PNGs are refused with a message naming the file. Any size: an image is
  stretched over the tile (tiles should be square) or the sprite's footprint. Alpha is transparency
  where the original has its transparent colour 0: on flat (see-through) faces, sprites and slope sides;
  opaque faces draw the colour regardless.
- Images much larger than the scale can show are box-filtered down at load: tiles to 128 N texels, sprites
  to 2 N times their original size (so a 256 x 256 tile is drawn from 128 x 128 at `hires=1`).

### Variants: remaps and directions

The original draws one tile with different CLUTs: lids with the block's remap (ext bits 3-4, 0..3; mostly
shading, e.g. the shadowed pavement), sides with a CLUT per direction (0 top, 1 bottom, 2 left, 3
right). Sprites have a remap byte (cars: the colour of the car, peds: the clothes).

- `lid/<n>_r<r>.png`, `side/<n>_r<d>.png`, `aux/<n>_r<r>.png`: the image for that variant. Without it
  the plain image stands for variant 0 and the others are derived: each colour channel scaled the way the
  variant's CLUT scales the original tile on average.
- `sprite/<n>_r<r>.png`: the image for remap r.
- `sprite/<n>_mask.png`, the **paint mask** convention for remapped sprites (cars): white where the image
  is paint, black elsewhere (grey blends). For remap r the masked pixels take the paint colour the remap
  gives the original (the average remapped colour of the texels the remap changes), shaded by the skin
  pixel's brightness relative to the original paint's average. Without a mask or an `_r` image, every
  remap shows the plain image.
- Damage and door deltas don't apply to skin sprites (the plain image is drawn whatever the delta mask).

## The sample skin

`assets/skins/sample` is generated by `tools/make-sample-skin.py` (Python stdlib) from code alone: no
game file is read, and its `skin.ini` says so. It replaces, in style 1, lid 1 (road), lid 8 (a pavement),
lid 41 and aux 25-35 (water and its animation frames), side 138 (a wall) and sprite 72 (the car parked at
mission 1's start, with a paint mask), at 256 x 256 (the car 248 x 256), and leaves everything else to the
original art. It writes its PNGs as RGB, palette + `tRNS` and RGBA, with all five row filters, to
exercise the decoder.

```sh
python3 tools/make-sample-skin.py           # regenerates assets/skins/sample
./build/skin_test                           # decoder, stack and fallback checks, renders in out/skins/
```

## Implementation

`src/render/hires/hires_skin.c` (loader, overlay layer), `hires_png.c` (decoder, on `src/inflate.c`),
`hires_tex.c` (the overlay stack the city pass asks: skin n ... skin 1, then the original art). Each skin
caches what it found and what it didn't, so a missing file is probed once. A layer answers a
`HiresAsset` (style, kind, number, variant, the CLUT the original would use and its variant-0 CLUT, the
original texels), so other kinds of layer (an upscaler over the original art, a pack in another format)
fit the same hook.
